beats.headline: In the Princess Posse
beats.text: Carl and Donut are in the Meadowlark saferoom, and Tipid is telling it to them: fifty thousand of us under their banner, and I am one of them. People who got out of a crawl once and know exactly what one is, and signed up for another anyway, under the banner of a cat. He gets emotional about it. Nobody gives him a hard time. We had the same faces on when we signed.

beats.headline: It is done
beats.text: The throne rooms lock in place, and every one of them shows on the map now. Carl asks in chat whether I had ours prepared before it locked. It is done. The rest of the project I am building with the sluggalos. They do not mind the idea of accidentally tripping a trap and being skewered. It is not finished yet.

beats.headline: Contingencies upon contingencies
beats.text: Carl worries that closing the saferoom cuts me off from his sapper's table and the bomber's studio. I already have everything I need. It's safer and faster to use his table, but there is nothing left I can't do on my own. He worries the worms learned our secrets. It doesn't matter. I pull a thread, and the folded papers around me come together into a spiral. I have contingencies heaped upon contingencies. Have faith in the process. Danger lives in what they can't see.

beats.headline: The slug that is not a slug
beats.text: I send the sluggalos up to the surface, all but one. Sick-Ass Worgo. Tell your real boss we need to talk. Juice Box. I noticed the change the moment the real Worgo went down the new tunnel and came back a few minutes after: body temperature, weight, no hormonal emissions. I chose the slugs because I assumed the changelings could not copy them. I was wrong. There are traps between us I placed myself. She counts six. There are eight. She changes, and the head becomes Juice Box's. Underneath us, a digger is moving. I ask her to call it off.

beats.headline: Dante, and the ice elves
beats.text: I tell her why. Long ago I killed a trap store's proprietor out of anger, and dozens of crawlers died for want of supplies. After the crawl, as an indentured merchant, my neighbour was a crocodilian named Dante. One season we were castle guards, and we were ordered to kill the ice elves inside, gentle creatures who loved puzzles and the snow. Dante refused twice, and a beam erased him. I refused once. I lost a wing. Then I did it, because I was afraid. I am still not free. But Dante taught me there is no such thing as the point of no return.

beats.headline: Get them under three thousand
beats.text: Tipid activates the base defences just in time. Two or three battalions of Dreamers have teleported in outside the FUPA and are running for the throne room, and Rosetta thinks it is all of them. That is too many. I ask her to chop them up a little first and get them down under three thousand. Then we let them in. I will welcome any and all guests into my lair. I would have preferred Reavers. I will take what I can get.

beats.headline: We need that gate back
beats.text: We need to move on the war mages now. They have the Gate. I do not understand why they are not allied with the other NPCs, and I do not understand why that Residual is their warlord. We do not know their plans. Rosetta is ready to let them win and be done with it. I am not done yet. Rosetta, you are the most stubborn person I have ever known. Trust me in this. We need that gate back, and we need to move before the defensive towers spin up.

beats.headline: I know the merchant
beats.text: I tell them again. Get the gate back and none of it will matter. Carl says he knows where it is. Tipid wants me to stay in the tunnels, and says they don't understand because I haven't told them what I need it for. I ask Carl again. He tells me: in the stomach of a merchant named Paca, in the Midnight Market. I know who that is. She is an ambassador for the dungeon's own version of the Apothecary. There have been seasons when my shop was inside that market. With the sluggalos, I will have it shortly.

beats.headline: He breaks the Nothing
beats.text: Crawler Justice Light did not take the stairs with the rest of you. He hid, stayed on this side of the veil, and snapped a piece of twine. A Legendary Trap has been triggered: a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap, dropped into the permanent portal the Gate of the Feral Gods had become. All captured bijou have been freed. All captured evicted demons have been freed. The Nothing has been broken, and it is draining into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol and into Scolopendra's Lair. Scolopendra stirs. He did not survive it. He knew that going in, and did not appear to require my opinion on the matter.

beats.headline: Dead, and the Nothing with him
beats.text: Welcome to the tenth floor. Some housekeeping before the fun. Crawler Justice Light is dead. The Nothing is broken. Those are two sentences I have never had cause to put next to each other, and I would like it understood that I am saying them under protest. Five thousand five hundred and one of you remain. Proceed.
